questions.question: Which generation produces spores in archegoniates ?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: Sporophytic generation
  • Evergreen Nature: Most gymnosperms retain their leaves throughout the year, providing consistent color
  • in gardens.
  • Theca (Main Body): The central part where spores are produced. It consists of
  •  Wall/Jacket: The capsule wall is 4-5 layers thick. The epidermis is thick-walled, with no stomata
  • present, a key feature in distinguishing Pogonatum from closely related Polytrichaceae.
  •  Spore Sac: A cylindrical, chambered spore sac exists between the outer wall and the inner columella.
  •  Columella: A central, sterile column of parenchyma cells that extends from the apophysis to the
  • operculum.
  • General Structure and Morphology
  • The strobilus of Selaginella is a small, terminal, spike-like structure. It is usually found on the tip of lateral
  • branches, though in some species, the stem continues to grow beyond the strobilus, where a fertile zone is
  • interspersed with vegetative leaves. The core axis of the strobilus is a continuation of the stem, often called
  • the strobilar axis, which bears sporophylls in close proximity, creating a compressed, dense appearance
  • compared to the leafy stem.Sporophylls are modified leaves that are typically similar in appearance to
  • ordinary vegetative leaves but are slightly smaller and more pointed. They are generally arranged spirally or
  • in four longitudinal rows along the central axis.
  • Ligule: A small, membranous structure called a ligule is present on the adaxial surface of every sporophyll
  • at its base, located between the ligule pit and the sporangium.
  • Sporophyte (Dominant Phase)
  • The palm like plant body is the diploid sporophyte which is dioecious
  • Male Plant -Produces a large cone called a microsporangiate strobilus which contains microsporophylls
  • bearing microsporangia.
  • Female Plant-Does not form a true cone (unlike many gymnosperms) and bears megasporophylls arranged
  • in a rosette at the apex. Each megasporophyll carries ovules (megasporangia) on its margins.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: in a rosette at the apex. Each megasporophyll carries ovules (megasporangia) on its margins.

questions.question: Name one type of cell seen in pericycle of Pinus needles.
questions.solution_html:
• Ans:A form of asexual reproduction where the plant body breaks into pieces, and each fragment develops
  • into a new individual.
  • Foliage Diversity: From the needle-like leaves of pines to the fan-shaped leaves of Ginkgo, they offer
  • varied textures.
  • Operculum and Peristome: The operculum is the lid, often with a rostrate (beaked) apex, covering the
  • capsule. The mouth is surrounded by 32 or sometimes 64 short, triangular, and dark-colored
  • peristome teeth.
  • Arrangement within the Strobilus
  • The arrangement of microsporophylls and megasporophylls inside the strobilus varies by species
  • In many species, microsporophylls and megasporophylls are mixed irregularly throughout the strobilus.
  • Insome species like S. kraussiana or S. rupestris, the megasporophylls are restricted to the base of the
  • strobilus, while the upper portion consists entirely of microsporophylls.Most Selaginella species have
  • bisporangiate strobili (containing both types). However, in some species the strobili are unisporangiate
  • meaning a single strobilus produces only one type of spore.
  • (Description 7 marks+ labelled diagram (3marks))
  • Pollination
  • Pollination is usually wind-assisted (sometimes insect-aided). Pollen grains reach the ovule through the
  • micropyle. A pollination drop helps to capture pollen.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: micropyle. A pollination drop helps to capture pollen.

questions.question: What is peat moss?
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The progressive dominance and independence of the sporophyte is a fundamental evolutionary trend
  • in archegoniates (bryophytes, pteridophytes, and gymnosperms). This involves a shift from a short-lived
  • dependent sporophyte in bryophytes to a dominant, free-living sporophyte in vascular plants, allowing for
  • better colonization of land.
  • Dependent Sporophyte in Bryophytes -In bryophytes (liverworts and mosses), the sporophyte
  • is physically attached to the gametophyte and relies on it entirely or partially for nutrition and water
  • Transition towards Independence in hornworts- This group shows a crucial intermediate step where the
  • sporophyte has an intercalary meristem (allowing continuous growth) and is photosynthetic.
  • Progressive Dominance & Independence in Pteridophytes- The sporophyte is perennial and showing
  • unlimited growth and completely independent of the gametophyte
  • Ultimate Dominance in Gymnosperms and Angiosperms- The gametophyte is extremely reduced (e.g.
  • pollen grains and embryo sac) and relies entirely on the sporophyte for survival and the dominant
  • sporophyte is perfectly adapted to dry environments
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: sporophyte is perfectly adapted to dry environments

questions.question: Explain progressive dominance and independence of the sporophyte in archegoniates
questions.solution_html:
• Ans: The progressive dominance and independence of the sporophyte is a fundamental evolutionary trend
  • in archegoniates (bryophytes, pteridophytes, and gymnosperms). This involves a shift from a short-lived
  • dependent sporophyte in bryophytes to a dominant, free-living sporophyte in vascular plants, allowing for
  • better colonization of land.
  • Dependent Sporophyte in Bryophytes -In bryophytes (liverworts and mosses), the sporophyte
  • is physically attached to the gametophyte and relies on it entirely or partially for nutrition and water
  • Transition towards Independence in hornworts- This group shows a crucial intermediate step where the
  • sporophyte has an intercalary meristem (allowing continuous growth) and is photosynthetic.
  • Progressive Dominance & Independence in Pteridophytes- The sporophyte is perennial and showing
  • unlimited growth and completely independent of the gametophyte
  • Ultimate Dominance in Gymnosperms and Angiosperms- The gametophyte is extremely reduced (e.g.
  • pollen grains and embryo sac) and relies entirely on the sporophyte for survival and the dominant
  • sporophyte is perfectly adapted to dry environments

  • molecular-based taxonomic system for extant ferns and lycophytes. It organizes these plants based on
  • monophyletic relationships, recognizing two distinct classes: Lycopodiopsida (Lycophytes like club mosses
  • spike mosses,etc.) and Polypodiopsida (horsetails, ferns,etc), covering 51 families and over 11,900 species.
